issues.title: 'cancellation_reason' predicts 'churned' on its own at 0.99
issues.detail: A depth-3 tree on 'cancellation_reason' alone recovers the label 99% of the time, against 56% for always guessing the biggest class. A single column this accurate is not a strong feature, it is the answer copied into the input, usually written after the outcome was known. Anything trained with it will score well here and fail on new data.

issues.title: 50 rows appear on both sides of 'split'
issues.detail: 50 rows appear identically on both sides of 'split'. Anything measured on this split is measuring memorisation. This is the failure that produces a high validation score with nothing in the training curve to warn you, so it is worth fixing before anything else on this list.

issues.title: 39 rows have a label the model disagrees with
issues.detail: 39 rows carry a label the model disagrees with, having never seen those rows during training. Cross-validated accuracy is 0.99, so the model is worth listening to. The most confident disagreements are ranked first.

issues.title: 20 near-duplicate row pairs
issues.detail: 20 pairs of rows agree on every field but one, covering 40 rows. Most commonly 'tenure_months' differs slightly. Near-copies usually come from a re-import or a partial edit, and they weight the same record twice.

issues.title: 'plan' has 1 value spelled more than one way
issues.detail: ' Premium ', 'PREMIUM', 'Premium', 'premium' are the same value written differently, and every model will treat them as separate categories. 93 rows use a non-canonical spelling.

issues.title: 12 outlying values in 'tenure_months'
issues.detail: 12 rows sit far outside the rest of 'tenure_months'. The most extreme is 6900 against a median of 37. Measured against median absolute deviation, so a few large values cannot inflate the threshold and hide inside it.
